text: unverified: the Claim's second half, "two hands of the same strength split it", is only half-dischargeable here. This diff settles the evaluator side of it — equal ranks produce an equal integer whatever the suits (`site/wwyhd-eval.js` uses suit only in the flush predicate, pinned by leg (j)'s two-wheel equality) — but nothing in this patch divides a pot, because the pot lives in the engine, a SIBLING FILES path (`site/wwyhd-engine.js`, task 3). What would settle it: a case in `tools/wwyhd-engine.test.ts` that gives two seats hands of equal `evaluate` score and asserts the chips are split between them. Graded minor and non-blocking: no edit inside this task's FILES could carry it, and every Machine clause M1 to M5 is fully discharged by the green exam.

undeclared amendment: the task Context pins the import as `import { evaluate } from "./wwyhd-eval.js"` and INTERFACES lists only `evaluate(cards: string[]): number` as Consumes, but site/wwyhd-rules.js:35 imports a second symbol, `import { evaluate, handCategory } from "./wwyhd-eval.js"`, and postflopBand keys its monster/two-pair tests on `handCategory(evaluate(all))` (site/wwyhd-rules.js:234-235). No AMENDMENTS entry declares reading that clause more widely. The choice itself is sound - `handCategory` is a documented public export of site/wwyhd-eval.js (its CATEGORIES array is named there as the contract) and keying on names is cleaner than decoding the score encoding by hand - so no code change is needed

what is missing is the declaration. Fix by adding an AMENDMENTS entry (`clause`: the Context's import line is read as naming the module, not the exhaustive symbol list) rather than by rewriting the import.

Preflop, `decide` folds before it ever looks at whether a check is free: site/wwyhd-rules.js:442-448 returns `fold()` as soon as `preflopPercentile(view.cards) > profile.vpip`, and the `if (toCall <= NO_AMOUNT) return check()` guard at site/wwyhd-rules.js:455 sits below that branch. So an opponent in an unopened big blind (toCall 0, legal.check true) folds a hand outside its vpip instead of checking for nothing - a seat giving up a free hand, which the engine will render to the visitor as a player folding when they owe zero chips. Nothing in the exam catches it because the only preflop fixture, UNOPENED_PRE, has toCall 200 and check false. Note the tension: M3 literally says "fold when not entering", so this is a faithful transcription and I am not calling it a plan-defect

it is a real-play wart worth a guard. A one-line fix inside this task's own FILES, which changes no graded case: in the preflop branch, before the vpip test, `if ((view.toCall ?? 0) <= 0 && view.legal.check === true) return check();`.

unverified: the rules table's fit with the engine that will call it (site/wwyhd-engine.js, a SIBLING FILES path this patch does not touch) cannot be settled here. Two specific edges: (1) `decide` detects "a bet is in front of me" from `view.toCall` alone (site/wwyhd-rules.js:428, 455) rather than from `view.legal`, so it depends on the engine populating `toCall` as the chips this seat owes, zero when nothing is owed

(2) the table never returns type "bet" - it checks instead (site/wwyhd-rules.js:455) and returns "raise" even for a preflop open into the blinds (site/wwyhd-rules.js:444-446) - so an engine that only accepts "bet" where no wager is outstanding would reject that action. The exam's own `expectLegal` also reads `legal.call` as a chip count (`toBeGreaterThan(0)`, tools/wwyhd-rules.test.ts:704) rather than a boolean, which is a guess about Task 3's `legalActions` shape. What would settle it: an engine-side test that drives a hand through `decide` and applies the returned actions, asserting chip conservation - Task 1's or Task 3's exam, not this one.

concern: plan-defect: Proof leg (a) grades state internals ("B at 2900 with 100 in", "every player has 25 more in", "A to act") but the task's Produces list pins no field names for State, so a peer exam's spelling and mine may differ. The engine names them: seat `stack`, seat `committed` (this street's contribution, ante excluded, which is what a bet or raise amount counts up to), seat `in` (everything put in this hand, ante included, which is what "25 more in" measures and what side pots are built from), `state.pot`, `state.toAct` (the handle) and `state.toActIndex`. A red leg (a) is most likely this naming rather than the dealing itself, which my own copy of the exam exercises.

Privacy edge the Machine clauses do not cover: for a stranger who submits a valid email with an empty or whitespace-only `displayName`, the consumed `resolveDisplay` (functions/api/_lib.js:18) falls back to `String(email).split("@")[0]`, so the public GET leaderboard publishes the email's local part (e.g. `john.smith` for `john.smith@gmail.com`). This passes M5 (the body carries no `@`) and matches the RSVP behaviour the task's Context told the implementer to clone, so the diff is not wrong here, but the Global Constraint 'no email in any GET response' arguably intends more than the `@` test. The fix is outside this task's FILES (it would mean a `resolveDisplay` change in functions/api/_lib.js, or a Machine clause saying the stranger fallback is the ANONYMOUS constant already defined at functions/api/wwyhd.js as `player`), so it is the plan's call, not the implementer's.

The task's Context asserts a `wrangler pages dev` probe on 2026-09-20 did so for ../../site/engine.js, which is strong but is not this diff's evidence. What would settle it: a `wrangler pages dev` (or `wrangler pages deploy --dry-run`) probe that GETs /api/wwyhd?hand=<id> and gets a computed chips value back rather than a bundling error. Graded minor because no edit inside this tree can demonstrate it.

M1 requires validateHandFile to throw for "a seat whose `profile` is not null", but tools/lib/wwyhd.ts exempts `undefined` as well as `null` (`if (player.profile !== null && player.profile !== undefined)`). Since JSON cannot carry an explicit `undefined`, the practical effect is that a hand file which simply omits the seat's `profile` key validates and is cast to `HandFile`, whose declared shape is `profile: HandProfile | null`. Leg (e) only covers the explicit-profile case, so nothing catches this. The consequence is downstream: the seat is the one player identified by a null profile, and a consumer written as `player.profile === null` (the natural reading of the type this task Produces) would fail to recognise the visitor's seat on such a file. Every required leg is satisfied and the exam is green, so this is advisory rather than blocking. Note that the opponent branch is already strict (`if (!profile || typeof profile !== "object")`), so only the seat is lenient.

unverified-by-exam Context/copy-rule gap: the reveal names real players by handle only. The task's Context says "the reveal names real players as `First L.` from `data.players[].name` looked up through `aka`, beside the handle", and the Copy-rules global constraint says real players are "named First + last initial from games.json beside their handle" on every generated puzzle page. The static sit-down markup satisfies this (tools/render.ts `wwyhdSeat` prints `wwyhdName(data, handle)` beside `esc(player.handle)`), but the runtime reveal does not: `holdingsList()` in site/wwyhd.js emits `${seat.handle}: ${cards} (${note})` and nothing else on the reveal carries a First L. name. The controller cannot derive one today — `HandFile["players"][number]` in tools/lib/wwyhd.ts carries only `handle`, and the embedded JSON is the whole hand file, so no name map reaches the browser. No Machine clause or Proof leg pins the reveal's naming, and the constraint carries no `Check:`, so this is minor rather than blocking. Cheapest fix with no schema change: have `holdingsList()` read the name already printed in the seat row, e.g. `document.querySelector(`[data-handle="${h}"] .wwyhd-who`)?.firstChild?.textContent?.trim()`, and fall back to the handle when absent
alternatively have renderWwyhdHand emit a `<script type="application/json" id="names">` handle→name map.

Comment contradicts behavior in site/wwyhd.js `leaderboardTable`: the doc comment says "the visitor's own row underneath when it is not already up there", but the "You" row is appended unconditionally, so a visitor inside the top ten is listed twice (once by display name, once as "You"). The GET contract as documented in the file header returns `leaderboard: [{name, chips}]` with no marker identifying the visitor, so de-duplication is not actually implementable client side — the comment is the thing that is wrong. Given the repo's comment-accuracy constraint ("every exported function carries a comment saying what it takes, returns and throws"), align the prose with what the code does.

Stale counts left in tools/site.test.ts, a file this diff modifies and whose count the task explicitly asked to correct. The diff extends `watched` to seven entries and updates the test title to "the seven generated paths", but two neighbouring comments still say six: line 863 ("an UNCOMMITTED hand-edit to any of the six watched paths"), which describes that very array, and lines 811-812 ("None of the six paths render.ts owns exist in the copy afterwards ... but the five that have nothing to do with the archive") in the malformed-archive block. Nothing fails because of it
it is comment drift in the one file the task asked to keep honest about this number.
